💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Apple unveiled its inaugural folding phone, the iPhone Duo, it pretty much met expectations — but the biggest drawback was the firm's decision to revert to Touch ID from Face ID, which felt like a huge step down for some.
  • However, the latest iOS 27.3 developer beta patches over this pain point, and owners of the Apple foldable can now unlock their devices with Face ID.
  • Sources indicate that for the most part, the iPhone Duo's upcoming facial recognition tool functions very similarly to the Face ID feature we all know, allowing you to unlock your device from your lock screen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Apple unveiled its inaugural folding phone, the iPhone Duo, it pretty much met expectations — but the biggest drawback was the firm's decision to revert to Touch ID from Face ID, which felt like a huge step down for some.

However, the latest iOS 27.3 developer beta patches over this pain point, and owners of the Apple foldable can now unlock their devices with Face ID.

Sources indicate that for the most part, the iPhone Duo's upcoming facial recognition tool functions very similarly to the Face ID feature we all know, allowing you to unlock your device from your lock screen. But because of the foldable's limited hardware support, it's not as robust as Face ID.

Recent findings suggest that before you get excited about the iPhone Duo's new software upgrade, there are a few limitations to bear in mind. Firstly, the camera-based facial recognition tool doesn't survive on its own, and still requires the help of Touch ID. If you want to unlock your iPhone Duo using facial recognition, it requires you to have recently used Touch ID or your device's passcode within a 45-minute window, so the two go hand-in-hand.

Sources indicate that as far as the upcoming facial recognition tool goes, it's only available to use on the Lock Screen, and doesn't have support for features like Apple Pay, passwords, logins, and other amenities that offer the same level of convenience. Presumably because of the Duo's folding hinge, numerous displays, and overall thinness, there's no room for a TrueDepth sensor, the dedicated tool that powers Face ID and all of its capabilities.

Still, it would've been the perfect opportunity for the company to take inspiration from the likes of Google Pixel phones.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

Though Google's smartphones also pack camera-based facial recognition, there's nothing that it can't do, be that making digital purchases, accessing passwords, signing into apps, and even organizing your photo gallery by the faces in each image.

In a recent development, that stated, while Pixel phones seem to have it all, camera-based facial recognition that's not supported by a sensor lacks a layer of security, making it much easier to bypass using 2D images of a subject. With sensor-based tools, it's much more difficult to achieve this, as they analyze and create a 3D map of the face, use detection tools to pick up facial liveliness, and pack infrared scattering tools so it can scan faces in darker environments.

It's still early days, however, and customers are only just getting used to a world in which Apple foldables exist. It could be that we'll have to wait until the iPhone Duo's third-gen model to see some improvements on this front — which may not arrive until 2028 at the earliest, according to Bloomberg's own Mark Gurman.

Words can be made from linked letters — up, down, left, right, or diagonal, but words can also change direction, resulting in quirky shapes and patterns. #1859. XREAL Aura Initial Review: Taking Android XR out of the headset, but who is it for?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2361 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5google ↗ Open Full Page

XREAL Aura Initial Review: Taking Android XR out of the headset, but who is it for?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2361 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, we all kind of want to be Tony Stark, don’t we?
  • XREAL isn’t newly introduced to the mixed reality space.
  • According to recent reports, XREAL Aura is a two-part device.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we all kind of want to be Tony Stark, don’t we? Almost everyone can relate to that futuristic sense of wonder that comes from the movies where we see digital elements being interacted with through a simple wave of the hand. To date, that’s only really been replicable through substantial ol’ headsets like Apple’s Vision Pro or the various Meta Quest sets. But with XREAL Aura, Android XR brings that feeling to something far easier to actually use, but my one remaining question is who this product is for.

XREAL isn’t newly introduced to the mixed reality space. The company has been building some of the best example of optical see-through XR glasses. These aren’t quite like a VR headset because they actually let you see the world around you, not through a camera, but by simply making the lenses themselves see-through. I’ve tried these in the past and, while they’re great for mirroring a tablet or laptop for bigger screen (especially on airplanes), I did feel they were missing something.

But first, let’s talk hardware.

According to recent reports, XREAL Aura is a two-part device. There are the glasses themselves which include two displays, one for each eye, and electrochromic dimming on the lenses to control just how much of the outer world you’re seeing. It’s wildly different from a typical VR headset, while also having most of the same benefits. Unlike most other XREAL glasses, Aura has built-in world-facing cameras used for hand and spatial tracking, as well as being able to be used as a camera for things like scanning QR codes, Gemini Live, or simply taking a quick picture (there’s no privacy light here, but the bulkier-than-normal design compared to standard glasses is more than enough a dead giveaway that the “perv glasses” dilemma doesn’t really apply in my opinion).

The other half of the formula is a wired puck that provides battery power and the brains of Android XR. There’s no screen on the puck, just a status light, and it has USB-C out for the glasses as well as USB-C in for power and/or external devices. It also has a fingerprint sensor (are you hearing this Android tablet makers??) and a touchpad, the latter used as a secondary, far subtler input method within Android XR to supplement hand tracking.

Sources indicate that together, these two make a wonderful package for building a true mixed reality experience. The displays are plenty bright for even the brightest indoor conditions (frankly, it’d be insane to use these outside in my opinion, though a wide-open plane window may present a challenge), and the electrochromic dimming does a great job of blocking out most, but not quite all of the world around you. If you’re looking to be fully cut off from reality as you would with a VR headset, these aren’t for you. I did find some display elements, like smaller text, a little tough to focus my eyes on at times, but I have a feeling that’s more so me being overdue for an eye exam than it is the glasses themselves. There’s virtually no flicker in my usage, with only bright white backgrounds occasionally being a little overbearing, and everything is smooth with the 120Hz refresh rate.

Where this hardware really shines compared to a typical VR headset is in its design, and it’s what makes XREAL a perfect partner for Android XR. The glasses themselves weigh in at 95 grams, a mere fifth of the Meta Quest 3 and Samsung’s Galaxy XR, and up to 700 grams less than Apple’s Vision Pro. It’s comfortable for much longer periods of time and not nearly as annoying to actually put on either, as it just feels like putting on a pair of bulky sunglasses. They look a little goofy, obviously, but far less so than a full-on VR headset like any of those mentioned above. This is also the only one of those I consider “mixed reality” thanks to the see-through lenses. Apple and Samsung constantly talk about Vision Pro and Galaxy XR as if they’re mixed reality, but a camera feed is explicitly not true reality. But XREAL’s glasses still aren’t quite just augmented reality, because they’re not just letting you see that digital world through a tiny window, they’re quite literally overlaying everything on top of the real world around you. The illusion is somewhat broken by the limited 70-degree field-of-view and the fact that darker backgrounds often look a little funky when there are light sources in the real world in front of you, but I can say with confidence that this is my favorite version of this experience – the speakers are pretty good too, topping it all off.

And that brings us to Android XR.

Industry observers note that google’s platform released on Samsung’s Galaxy XR headset earlier this year, and it’s all pretty familiar on XREAL Aura. The Android-based experience opens up to a floating launcher of your favorite apps that mostly open up into floating windows in front of you. You can use hand gestures to move everything around or interact with UI elements, and every app I tried worked perfectly well. The gestures can be hit or miss at times, especially the one for going back to the home screen (having this as a long-press that you have to physically look at your hand for gets annoying when doing anything remotely fast-paced, but thankfully the top button is a dedicated home shortcut), but it works well and everything is designed fairly intuitively. A floating cursor indicates where you are aiming with a pinch acting as a tap on a touchscreen, and you can move things around in your space as if they’re real objects. There’s a sense of depth throughout the entire experience.

Some apps open to fully immersive experiences, but these are still in the minority. XREAL touts that there are around 150 experiences launching alongside Aura, but it’s definitely still early days here. Apps like Google TV should obviously be ready for a full format like that but, most things, like the Google Docs app which I’m typing this review in right now, just act as if they’re on independent displays floating around you.

According to recent reports, like Googlebook, Android XR is also still struggling to figure out the best app experience for each user. Most things are mobile apps, including Google Chrome which is just the standard Android version from your phone. It’s fine in most cases, but I found this restrictive seeing as I can get a ton done in a browser, but fighting mobile optimization is a frustrating way to interact with a window that can be as major as a TV if you want it to. Meanwhile, the Spotify app is weirdly the web version which is horribly optimized for interacting with hand gestures. I’d have rather had the mobile version here. Another quirk I found was notifications, which pop up at the top of the display and quite literally on top of whatever you’re doing. Something they were invasive, and having to physically reach out to dismiss them is a little annoying. I’m sure there are workflows to help make this less of a distraction, but I’d almost rather have notifications turned off entirely.

According to recent reports, there’s also Gemini, which is core to the experience here. A quick “Hey Google” triggers a Gemini Live session for answering questions, and you can share what you’re seeing to give additional context. It’s way faster than switching between apps to get a quick search done, but there are friction points here, especially if you’re just asking a single question. Gemini answers swiftly and leaves the conversation going, great for follow-up queries, bad if you’re done because the UI controls go away, which leaves you to tell Gemini to end the session which, every time, it asks for secondary confirmation you want to end. Google, if I say “end the session,” I think that should be more than sufficient proof I want to end the session. Luckily, a long-press of the top home button fixes that headache, but I still hate that I either need to use a physical control, or basically have to fight an AI to end a conversation that I started hands-free.

Sources indicate that performance is excellent. Everything is smooth and quick, probably thanks in part to XREAL’s use of 12GB of RAM alongside Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite chip.

But how do you actually use a product like this?

Recent findings suggest that that’s the question I found myself asking when I first spun up XREAL Aura and started to learn its ins and outs. See, other XREAL glasses have an extremely straightforward use case. Plug in the external device of your choice, get it on a bigger screen. Simple, easy, obvious. I found this helpful in travel primarily, with a bigger display for my MacBook feeling nice for tasks like video editing, while the main value came in just having a very comfortable way to watch a movie on a flight from my connected tablet.

Recent findings suggest that both of those use cases are valid on XREAL Aura. You can plug a USB-C device into the puck to get that wired mirroring through an Android XR window, and it works super well. Having Android XR alongside that mirroring also opens the door to added functionality, like having extra windows off to the side for perhaps a media app or reference document if you run out of room on the wired device. As just one example, I kept Spotify and Slack open in side windows while using Aura with my MacBook Air for an afternoon of writing articles.

Industry observers note that I think Android XR makes Aura an absolute powerhouse for media consumption, as you can just download content directly to the device (256GB of storage in the base model) for a flight, or even just use streaming apps if you have Wi-Fi. I couldn’t find any 3D content during my brief review period (nothing in my Google TV library was compatible, apparently), but that’s also on the table. Genuinely, I cannot wait to use these on my next long flight.

But outside of those, I think a lot of the other scenarios start to fall apart.

By far the most popular use case for virtual/mixed reality has been gaming. XREAL Aura has a ton of potential here and I’m really excited to try out Project Hail Mary: Journey to the Stars on this, but the fact that these are simply glasses restricts a lot of what you can do. Any big movements could easily result in the glasses slipping or even falling off, whereas a VR headset is much more secure. Stationary immersive gaming has potential, and XREAL’s Gamesir controller collab indicates promise, but I’m just not sold on these as a replacement to something like Meta Quest seeing as the latter already has a deep catalog of games and a much more affordable price.

In a recent development, the other use case is productivity, one I’m also not entirely sold on. As mentioned, this entire post was written in Aura, and I’m not sure I benefitted much from that experience versus just using a normal laptop or desktop computer. My workflow was having Google Docs up in the center, typing on a physical keyboard (only a psycho could use the virtual keyboard for anything beyond the shortest messages or passwords) with reference documents in Chrome off to my right and Slack on my left, with the occasional “Hey Google” command helping to find information on the fly (such as the weight comparison earlier). It all works well, but I think Android XR is inherently limited by its reliance mostly on mobile apps, and also just by the use of gestures. You can use a mouse or trackpad, of course, but at that point you might as well just use a laptop.

According to recent reports, XREAL Aura is for a very specific customer from my point of view. Wired mirroring is still very much the strong suit here, with Android XR’s apps and offline video giving these utility outside of just relying on another device. That was my problem with previous XREAL glasses, because the experience just varies wildly depending on what’s connected. Aura’s puck and Android XR experience solves every complaint I had about previous models, while expanding very much on what it can do.

Further limiting matters is the price. $1,279, in my book, is actually a mostly fair price for this, especially given the RAMageddon of it all. XREAL 1+ Pro come in around $600 and is utterly useless without a secondary device. XREAL Aura more or less doubles the price, but includes the best possible version of that secondary device while also giving you the added camera sensors that are only available as add-ons for other hardware. Don’t get me wrong, it’s still pricey, but I don’t think it’s unfair either, especially not when one of the main competitors for this sort of experience is still $3,600 (which still sounds insane two years later, even for Apple).

It has been revealed that we’ll have far more to say about XREAL Aura in a long-term review from our Nick Sutrich, but the verdict on day one is that Android XR has really solved the biggest problem for XREAL, while XREAL has solved a lot of massive problems for Android XR, all while being an overall win for the user at the end of the day. Not so often we get a storybook ending like that in tech anymore, and I’m all here for it.

In a recent development, don’t forget, XREAL Aura is $200 off – so $1,099 – through the end of December. Much more worth it at that price.

The arrival of the latest flagship Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max might be dominating the headlines, but the Chinese smartphone giant also just lifted the curtain on a range of accessories that are worth paying attention to.

If you're a fan of open-ear audio, then the newly introduced Xiaomi Clip earbuds are going to be the start of the new reveals. They're the brand's first clip-on model, and weigh just 5.5g per earbud.

If you're not familiar with this relatively recent trend, clip-on earbuds attach to your ears with a gentle clamping mechanism rather than being pushed inside your ear canal like conventional buds. This makes them highly comfortable and leaves your ear canals open to allow in background noise like traffic or conversations.

They're not a good fit for a loud commute, but such designs have become a popular choice for fitness or scenarios where you want to maintain full situational awareness while still being able to enjoy some tunes.

Xiaomi promises that the Clip earbuds will feel like they're "barely there" while in use, and accommodate a wide range of ear shapes thanks to their flexible shape-memory alloy bridge material.

In a recent development, fashion is clearly a focus, and the Xiaomi Clip earbuds are offered in four distinct colorways: Sand Gold, Pearl White, Graphite Black, and Frost Purple. They all come with a compact charging case that's designed to look something like a jewelry box.

As for the more technical specs, each bud contains an 11mm dynamic driver. They offer Hi-Res certified sound and support the modern LHDC 5.0 codec. According to Xiaomi, the battery life comes in at 9 hours of music playback, with an additional 29 hours offered by the charging case.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

They cost £129.99 and are available via the Mi website.

There's no better companion for a new Android smartphone than a compatible smartwatch, and Xiaomi has you covered there too with the new Watch S5 41mm.

It has been revealed that this £199.99 smartwatch boasts a 1.32 AMOLED display with up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness. It runs Xiaomi HyperOS 4 and is the first Xiaomi Watch S model compatible with Google Wallet – so you can conveniently pay with your wrist without the need for Xiaomi Pay.

It comes packed with a range of sensors, including a heart rate sensor with blood oxygen sensing capabilities, an accelerometer, gyroscope, ambient light sensor, and temperature sensor. Xiaomi also states that the watch can last up to 14 days on a single charge.

Sources indicate that it's available in three color options: Black, Light Blue, and Ceramic White. Black and Light Blue both offer stainless steel bezels and rubber straps, while Ceramic White has a ceramic bezel and comes with a leather strap.

Sources indicate that finally, Xiaomi is refreshing its affordable smart band. The Xiaomi Smart Band 11 starts at just £54.99 and offers a bright 1.72-inch AMOLED display and the ability to read notifications and see call alerts, in addition to tracking your fitness.

There is a wide range of color options available, with different build materials depending on what you pick. The standard Midnight Black, Glacier Silver, Mystic Rose, and Moon Gold models feature an aluminum frame.

If you want a band with NFC capabilities, you can also pick up the crisp white ceramic edition or a full-metal unibody model in lavender.

Connections can be played on both web browsers and mobile devices and require players to group four words that share something in common.

Recent findings suggest that each puzzle features 16 words and each grouping of words is split into four categories. These sets could comprise of anything from book titles, software, country names, etc. Even though multiple words will seem like they fit together, there's only one correct answer.

If a player gets all four words in a set correct, those words are removed from the board. Guess wrong and it counts as a mistake—players get up to four mistakes until the game ends.

Players can also rearrange and shuffle the board to make spotting connections easier. Additionally, each group is color-coded with yellow being the easiest, followed by green, blue, and purple. Like Wordle, you can share the results with your friends on social media.

According to recent reports, if you picked up a newly introduced iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo this fall, or you’re shopping for someone with an iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch, there’s a good chance you’ve been holding out on purchasing accessories until all of the Black Friday deals started. We’ve got you covered with some great deals on premium accessories for nearly every Apple device on your list.

ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile. Here’s a look at what’s included in ESR’s Black Friday lineup and who each one is for.

In a recent development, if someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right. As we’ve seen with Android foldables, you’re protecting two halves, a hinge, and a phone that changes shape throughout the day as you use it, all without adding bulk to a device people bought because it folds thin. ESR has two options for iPhone Duo owners, and the choice mostly comes down to the look you want to achieve.

Sources indicate that the ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand is your choice if you want to show off your iPhone Duo’s colors. It combines a rigid polycarbonate and acrylic back with a softer TPU frame. The rigid back keeps the case from flexing and lets the iPhone Duo’s design show through, while the flexible frame absorbs the shock if you drop it (please don’t).

The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand is perfect for those who want a more premium look for their iPhone Duo. It’s made from organic silicone leather with a soft, skin-friendly feel and a stain-resistant finish. If you’ve ever used a light-colored leather case before, you know it usually shows every stain and smudge it comes across, but ESR built the Atelier to resist daily wear and wipe clean.

Recent findings suggest that both cases share ESR’s Flex Stand, and it’s one of the most innovative and versatile parts of the lineup. It’s a 180-degree rotating stand made from zinc alloy, so it holds its shape even after months of propping up your iPhone. A precision hinge with damping control lets it open smoothly and lock at the angle you choose, whether the iPhone Duo is folded or unfolded, and ESR notes it has passed 3,000 open-and-close tests. In real life, that means propping the iPhone Duo open on a desk for a video call or on an airplane tray table for a movie, then using the stand as a grip when you’re holding it.

Recent findings suggest that both cases add extra hinge protection and raised edges where a foldable is most exposed. If you follow our MagSafe Monday column, you know magnetic strength really matters for MagSafe wallets, car mounts, etc. The Classic Hybrid has 1,500g of magnetic hold, and the Atelier has 1,400g.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case for iPhone Duo is 15% off.

The same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

According to recent reports, on these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

Recent findings suggest that protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

Industry observers note that why it matters: ESR indicates the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing demonstrates up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Installation is the part most people dread on a brand-newly introduced iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

Holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. An extra USB-C port lets a second device charge simultaneously. 9to5Mac’s Michael Burkhardt went hands-on with the Xtend 45W earlier this month and said it’s an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go.

It has been revealed that it’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR notes it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

In a recent development, for the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

According to recent reports, for a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

The trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the upcoming M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

Have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

When the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR says the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

According to recent reports, the result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Both cases also have 260g of magnetic strength, so they snap onto MagSafe chargers, Apple Watch chargers, and MagSafe batteries if you need to charge your AirPods. Again, it’s extremely strong, but extremely easy to unlock with one hand.

The ESR Cyber FlickLock Magnetic Case is extremely durable and has a clip hook, so you can hang your AirPods on a backpack while hiking or cycling. The ESR Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Case brings the same lock in a range of vibrant colors with a carrying lanyard, so you can wear your AirPods on your wrist or attach them to a bag. Both cases come in versions for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 and 1, and AirPods 5 and 4. No matter which AirPods you or your loved one have, this is the case everyone will love.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

In a recent development, the ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. It fits 44mm, 45mm, 46mm, and 49mm models across Apple Watch Ultra 1 through 4, Series 4 through 12, and SE 1 through 3, and it comes in several colors to match your outfit or your mood that day.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Equinox Watch Band is 20% off.

The best gifts are the ones that get used every day, and accessories are the part of the Apple experience people live with the most. A case that props up a foldable, a screen protector made with Corning glass, a charger with a built-in cable, and an AirPods case that stays closed even when dropped check all the boxes. ESR truly makes something for everyone and is one of the most trusted names in the Apple accessories ecosystem.

According to recent reports, ESR built its Black Friday lineup around the whole Apple ecosystem, from the new iPhone Duo to iPad, AirPods, and even a great Apple Watch band, with premium materials and versatile designs that are durable, functional, and great-looking. Sources indicate that what do you think of Samsung’s alleged Dynamic Island clone? Personally, I’m on board as long as it proves useful, and it seems to be on the right track compared to most other copycats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The deal would reportedly include newly introduced safeguards for younger owners, too.
  • Recent findings suggest that youTube could pay "around" $3 billion to thousands of US school districts to settle claims alleging the company's video platform harms the mental health of students, Bloomberg reports.
  • Like Meta, Snap and TikTok, YouTube is facing a growing number of lawsuits alleging that its platform is designed to be addictive, and that it knew using it could produce negative outcomes for younger users.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The deal would reportedly include newly introduced safeguards for younger owners, too.

Recent findings suggest that youTube could pay "around" $3 billion to thousands of US school districts to settle claims alleging the company's video platform harms the mental health of students, Bloomberg reports. The settlement "will likely take a few months to officially finalize" and is contingent on a majority of districts agreeing. The deal will reportedly also include "additional product safeguards for teens.".

Like Meta, Snap and TikTok, YouTube is facing a growing number of lawsuits alleging that its platform is designed to be addictive, and that it knew using it could produce negative outcomes for younger users. YouTube and many other Google products are heavily used in classrooms, so reaching a settlement would allow the company to avoid drawn-out legal battles during what's already a contentious moment between Google and schools. The districts themselves are seeking reimbursement for the counseling services they've had to supply to students, Bloomberg writes.

Sources indicate that meta, Snap, TikTok and YouTube settled an earlier lawsuit with a school district in Kentucky in May, in which YouTube agreed to pay slightly more than $2 million. The video platform was also found negligent in a personal-injury lawsuit in Los Angeles in March and agreed to settle a separate personal-injury lawsuit in June. A $3 billion settlement would be the largest ever reached with US school districts, according to Bloomberg, but still a fraction of the up to $18 billion Meta agreed to pay states in August.

Engadget has asked YouTube to comment on the school district settlement. We'll revision this article if we hear back.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that “Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Listening to the in-game radio stations while you cruise around in Grand Theft Auto VI, you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for.

Recent findings suggest that “Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.

It has been revealed that given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t major fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit newly introduced officers.

It’s a curious strategy given that the series rewards theft and drug dealing while enticing you to run over pedestrians, but evidently the mere presence of law enforcement in the games (as the primary antagonists, mind you) was enough to inspire waves of AI slop celebrating the thin blue line.

An Instagram channel of the San Diego Police Department, for example, on Thursday posted an AI-generated image of an SDPD cruiser set against a sunset over the San Diego Bay. Its neon pinks and purples match the saturated aesthetic of GTA, and in case there was any doubt what the department was going for, the nonsensical phrase “Join San Diego PD VI” appears at the top. “Want to drive a police car, we can make that happen!” reads the caption. “Apply Now!”.

Another police department in Washington state shared GTA-like imagery on its Instagram page, encouraging viewers to try “the real-life version” of GTA VI by pursuing a career in law enforcement. “No cheat codes,” the caption advertised. “No respawns. Just real people, real challenges, and a career that makes a difference.” A wave of self-serious GTA slop also flooded the feeds of police departments in Canada, from Edmonton to Toronto—though the Calgary Police Service tried something more lighthearted by having one of their traffic officers react to clips of dangerous and illegal driving maneuvers in the game.

Sources indicate that among police departments that were not seeking to add to their ranks through GTA VI fever, many posted content aimed at reminding people that laws exist in real life. “Keep It In The Game VI,” advised a typical post on the Instagram account of the Glendale Police Department in California, complete with a GTA-fied police cruiser and view of the city. “Follow posted speed limits, respect the law, and keep your wanted level at ZERO!” the caption warned. The Denver Police Department, in similarly scolding fashion, informed followers: “Grand theft auto is still illegal.”.

It has been revealed that the communications teams for these agencies should have perhaps reconsidered trying to farm engagement and clout from the massive success of GTA VI. As many commenters are noting, the game portrays cops as corrupt and quick to violence. Players have discovered that the Vice City squad will brutalize you if you start filming them during a questionable arrest. One clip showed a cop pulling his weapon on a character who had done nothing worse than stand in the street to take a selfie.

According to recent reports, A certain dose of this authoritarian cruelty ought to appeal to the right-wing cranks upset that GTA VI is too “woke” when it comes to gender, race, and politics overall. It’s a little different when the most visible villains of the game are choosing to overlook its vicious take on their profession in order to spam epic social media posts.

According to recent reports, fox News, just for comparison, dutifully took the tired law-and-order line on GTA VI, with talking heads aghast at kids’ exposure to virtual gun violence (never mind actual gun deaths in the US) and an atmosphere of moral depravity. Elon Musk famously declared that he couldn’t play GTA games because they compelled you to shoot cops.

It has been revealed that both stances, however insincere, suggest a modicum of regard for law enforcement that the police departments themselves immediately jettisoned in favor of GTA cringe. They of course won’t win any cool points for it, but at least this way they can pretend to connect with the general population.

More baffling still is that the Russian army has generated its own GTA VI recruitment ads to blast out on its Telegram channel, and NATO has trumpeted its defensive security alliance with military-industrial GTA sludge, boasting that “even the best gamers would have a challenge” eluding fighter jets and submarines. Trying to parse Vice President JD Vance’s depiction of a Trumpian “golden age” with GTA graphics is a fool’s errand. In the most dystopian development of all, a US Army battalion in Georgia granted 43 eligible soldiers four days off to play the fresh GTA in return for reenlisting for another two years of service.

What do any of these institutions or their missions have to do with a video game where you rob convenience stores in flip-flops? Doesn’t matter. When the zeitgeist is this all-consuming, you fire up ChatGPT and find an angle, no matter how confusing. Surely someone, somewhere, will be tricked into thinking you have anything to do with it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple is being sued in India by a U.S.-based startup that alleges the iPhone maker’s NameDrop feature, which lets consumers share contact information by bringing devices close together, infringes its patented technology.
  • GG Technologies, the startup behind StayTouch, an app that lets people exchange contact details by bringing their phones close together, is seeking ₹15 billion (about $161.86 million) in damages and an injunction against Apple, per court documents reviewed by TechCrunch.
  • Santa Monica-headquartered GG Technologies filed the lawsuit in India in October after mediation proceedings initiated in April failed in September, the startup told TechCrunch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is being sued in India by a U.S.-based startup that alleges the iPhone maker’s NameDrop feature, which lets consumers share contact information by bringing devices close together, infringes its patented technology.

GG Technologies, the startup behind StayTouch, an app that lets people exchange contact details by bringing their phones close together, is seeking ₹15 billion (about $161.86 million) in damages and an injunction against Apple, per court documents reviewed by TechCrunch.

Santa Monica-headquartered GG Technologies filed the lawsuit in India in October after mediation proceedings initiated in April failed in September, the startup told TechCrunch. Pre-institution mediation is generally required before filing commercial lawsuits in India. The company also sued Apple in the U.S. in April over related patent infringement claims.

In its 781-page court filing in the Bombay High Court, GG Technologies alleged that Apple’s NameDrop infringes its Indian patent on technology that helps phones exchange contact details with nearby devices without requiring manual pairing. The company introduced StayTouch in 2019, the same year it first sought patent protection for the technology in the U.S. It filed its Indian patent application in 2021 and received the patent in July 2024.

In a recent development, apple introduced NameDrop as part of iOS 17 in June 2023. The feature debuted on iPhones later that year, with support for compatible Apple Watches arriving in October through watchOS 10.1.

Recent findings suggest that “We are seeking an injunction to restrict the usage of the NameDrop feature which is native to iOS,” GG Technologies told TechCrunch. GG Technologies urged the court in its filing to restrict Apple from selling or importing iPhones and Apple Watches preloaded with NameDrop in India. The case has yet to be listed for a hearing.

It has been revealed that in the U.S., the International Trade Commission opened an investigation into Apple’s alleged patent infringement in August, following a complaint from GG Technologies. The startup is seeking an order that could block imports of infringing Apple devices into the country, along with restrictions on their sale.

Sources indicate that founded in 2018 by Gaurav Goel, a graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and a former Goldman Sachs investment banker, GG Technologies developed StayTouch as an alternative to exchanging business cards. The app is available on iOS and Android.

Apple did not respond to a request for comment.

It has been revealed that india has become increasingly important to Apple, both as a fast-growing consumer market and a major manufacturing hub outside China. The Cupertino firm has expanded its retail presence in the South Asian nation, where iPhones still account for less than 10% of smartphone shipments, giving considerable room for growth.

Breaking: Why you shouldn't depend on GTA 6 to auto-save

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In addition to getting your boss to let you take time off to play Grand Theft Auto 6, one of the more frightening prospects of playing games like GTA 6  is trusting the auto-save feature.
  • In a recent development, as ever, depending on auto save to make sure your journey through Vice City is like depending on Rockstar to release something rapidly.
  • If you're already tens of hours deep in your journey through the criminal underworld, it may be wise to stick around for a moment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In addition to getting your boss to let you take time off to play Grand Theft Auto 6, one of the more frightening prospects of playing games like GTA 6  is trusting the auto-save feature. It's been part of so many games for literal decades, but it's really found its home in massive, expansive open-world games like the GTA series. The old mantra of auto-save, then manual save twice just to be sure, still rings true today.

In a recent development, as ever, depending on auto save to make sure your journey through Vice City is like depending on Rockstar to release something rapidly. It's not a tremendously wise idea, and with GTA 6, Rockstar has implemented an auto save that certainly functions, but maybe not in the same way you may have grown accustomed to in other games.

If you're already tens of hours deep in your journey through the criminal underworld, it may be wise to stick around for a moment. Here's what we know about how the saving system works, and what you can do to make sure your progress isn't lost.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6's auto-save feature may not work as you think. Instead of automatically saving at regular intervals, the game appears to save after every main mission, as well as after some major side missions, expensive purchases, or when you get killed or arrested. That means if you're roaming the map, getting into trouble or driving around, the game relies on you to save manually. Unfortunately, the auto-save icon (a white spinning circle) doesn't always show up when the game saves.

GTA 6 has one auto-save slot, which it overwrites each time, and 15 manual slots. To manually save, press the Options button on PS5 or the Menu button on Xbox, then go to the Game tab and choose Save Game.

Industry observers note that the unusual auto-save system has caused several people to lose hours of progress, although in the bigger picture of a game that's sold in the millions, it's thankfully not too widespread. One save tip from our editors playing through the game: GTA 6 doesn't auto-save in the middle of a mission, period.

Industry observers note that if you're cruising the streets of Vice City and worry about a power outage, or if you're someone who turns the console off without thinking, remember to save manually. The same goes when you strike it significant and get your hands on the ride of your dreams or clear one of the countless side missions: Save regularly to keep your GTA 6 journey going and your sanity intact.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Moon is now a few days past its First Quarter phase, and we're well into the Waxing Gibbous stage, which means each night, a little more of its surface is illuminated. This pattern will continue until we reach the Full Moon.

As of Friday, Nov. 20, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 77% of its surface visible.

Recent findings suggest that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis and Tranquillitatis, as well as the Kepler Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Posidonius Crater, the Clavius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 11, 14, and 17 landing spots.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

According to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a Fresh Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

Fresh Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

According to recent reports, waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for children of the '80s and '90s, Don Bluth was a major influence on how we saw the world.
  • Social media is evergreen with fans remembering the tender moments of Littlefoot and his tree star, or the terrifying ones, like Fievel or Mrs.
  • Industry observers note that in an interview with Mashable, Bluth said watching the finished doc "brought tears to [his] eyes," because it refreshed memories of his colleagues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for children of the '80s and '90s, Don Bluth was a major influence on how we saw the world. With movies like The Secret of NIMH, An American Tail, The Land Before Time, All Dogs Go to Heaven, and Anastasia, this American animator offered us realms of adventure, with plucky heroes as well as villains so fantastically frightening that we carry the thrill of it all with us decades later.

Social media is evergreen with fans remembering the tender moments of Littlefoot and his tree star, or the terrifying ones, like Fievel or Mrs. Brisby being chased down by monstrous, roaring, ravenous cats. Now, for fans new and old, filmmakers Dave LaMattina and Chad N. Walker offer Don Bluth: Somewhere Out There, a documentary that explores the life and work of the innovative animator through his own words.

Industry observers note that in an interview with Mashable, Bluth said watching the finished doc "brought tears to [his] eyes," because it refreshed memories of his colleagues. Together, they pursued animation not for the money but for the art and a deep desire to create something meaningful for future generations. Yet, when asked about his legacy, Bluth is quick to look back on the path that led him to his work.

It has been revealed that he began by speaking of Winsor McCay, the father of American animation. In a wistful storyteller tone, Bluth recounted how a little boy witnessed the "magic" of the 1914 short film Gertie the Dinosaur, in which a pencil-sketched brontosaurus comes to life. This little boy was so inspired that he'd grow up to make his own animated short featuring a mouse named Mickey.

According to recent reports, that little boy, of course, was Walt Disney, who would go on to make 1937's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, the first animated feature film produced in the United States. That movie would go on to inspire a young Bluth, who'd direct his first animated feature in 1982 with The Secret of NIMH.

This path of inspiration to iconic art wasn't as direct a line as you might think.

Yes, Bluth scored a dream job, working at Disney Animation studio for 10 years on films like Sleeping Beauty, Robin Hood, and The Rescuers. But after Disney's death in 1966, Bluth and 17 other Disney animators feared the studio had lost their way, creatively.

He told Mashable he'd invite these artists to his home on weekends, where they'd draw together to develop innovative pitches for their corporate bosses. When they were shot down, Bluth — along with Gary Goldman and John Pomeroy — built their own manufacturer, Don Bluth Productions, to "see if we could do better than they were doing." For this, Bluth remembered, "We were called traitors.".

Recent findings suggest that that's not how Bluth saw his team. "[These] wonderful people had the courage to leave their jobs and security and go out there and try and do something great," he mentioned, "not just to feed their egos, but something they felt helped them grow up. And they wanted to give back.".

It has been revealed that it was not an easy journey, as Don Bluth: Somewhere Out There details, revealing the highs and lows of Bluth's most beloved and worst-reviewed productions, as well as the wildly popular video game Dragon's Lair. In our interview, he spoke repeatedly about how the doc filled him with gratitude as he looked back for the filmmakers' interviews.

Sources indicate that to Mashable, he reflected, "What happened after so many movies, All Dogs Go to Heaven, American Tail, working with Steven Spielberg on both of those pictures, and George Lucas [on The Land Before Time], [it] became really, really obvious to us that we were doing the right thing [by] writing the right stories, and trying to make something that would move people's lives for the better — not just to pat our own backs and say, 'Look what we did.' [We were making] something that would help maybe children grow up and have some degree of morality about them. So then, that was our goal in everything.".

In a recent development, in Somewhere Out There, the rise of computer animation — which Bluth refers to as "3D animation" — came as a devastating blow to the animator, who'd spent his life developing the skills of hand-drawn 2D animation. To this day, Bluth still advocates for the artistry of hand-drawn animation.

"The way I look at this is animation in the 2D form is people, armed with a pencil in their hands, have to be able to draw," he explained, "and they also have to be able to act. And they have to have feelings about story.".

According to recent reports, to Bluth, CGI movies aren't animation. "3D animation is puppetry," he stated, adding, "[With 3D animation,] you drop your pencil. You put your hands on a keyboard, and you make a wireframe puppet act.".

Bluth shared several of his complaints about the look of 3D animation, saying, "To me, it looks very plastic... The colors are muted, and they're trying to put shading in there, trying to look more like a live-action picture." He asked, "Why are we trying to get to a place which looks more real?" adding, "That isn't the purpose at all of 2D [animation]. The purpose is to take you to a magical world. 2D is trying to make audiences come to our own world.".

Noting the animation industry changed forever with the massive success of 1995's Toy Story, Bluth stated, "Toy Story [movies] were quite fun to watch, but they didn't make me feel anything very deep. And animation is intended to do that, particularly with Walt Disney pictures. Snow White, Bambi, [and] Pinocchio — those pictures did something to change the way you thought and help you grow up in a way that was really good. And they did it in such a beautiful way.".

It was when Disney Studios, post-Walt, moved away from these tenets that Bluth and his colleagues set out on their own. He said, "We left the Disney Studio because it was leaving out the morality statements and leaving out all the beautiful colors and everything.".

In terms of what recent animated films impressed Bluth, he mentioned, "I liked Klaus a lot," commending Sergio Pablos' inventive Christmas tale, which employs hand-drawn animation with a unique visual style.

Industry observers note that bluth also enjoyed Pete Docter's 2009 Pixar hit Up. "That was totally in 3D," he noted, "but it had a great story. For my taste, it went on too long. You know, the story was really about this couple promising each other they would go back to some place in their life, and she died. So, the man, true to the promise, tries to fulfill that [by taking their house on the journey]. So, I love that.".

Overall though, Bluth lamented, "Animation has become an advertisement for sugar cereal and whatever. There are more advertisements on animation than there are actually animated characters. The animated characters are just simply little puppets that jump up and down and tell one-line jokes. So, that's not good. Now, the last laugh is about to hit us like a tsunami; that is AI.".

Through the stories of Russian Jewish immigrant Fievel Mousekewitz, the widowed mother of four Mrs. Brisby, the orphaned brontosaurus Littlefoot, and rogue mutt Charlie B. Barkin, Bluth was striving to create stories that would inspire children to be good and creative, as Disney's movies had done for him. He doesn't see a future where AI can provide such mindful, moral guidance.

"It seems like AI is able to do wonderful, wonderful things," Bluth mused, "except AI is a machine, and it has no soul. It will borrow or steal, if you will, from everything that it knows, and give you what you ask for. But where's the creativity?".

"AI is a borrower," Bluth explained. "When you enter what you'd like to see, it searches all over and borrows it from other artists, puts it together. It indicates you on screen. Now, you can then make corrections. It can do all that, but it is still a machine. It doesn't ask you, 'Well, what is right and wrong? What is evil and good? What do you want me to say?' The machine can't do that.".

He continued, "The only thing you can do is go back to human beings and say, 'Don't replace human beings with machines.' They're the ones who have a heart, who have a soul, and probably have a Creator. So, there's a bigger picture that's going on than just animation on a screen.".

In a recent development, "AI has no soul," Bluth concluded. "It hasn't a clue how to write anything. Everything that you're going to see on your screen has been stolen from other artists.".

According to recent reports, he allowed that some AI might be "stunningly beautiful," but "you'll find that it doesn't affect your heart the way you feel… They're not artists that are doing the AI. Many of them don't understand the art of acting or anything. So, what everything looks like in AI animation that I've seen, it all looks like slow motion, and it looks unreal. So, that's definitely a road I don't want to travel on.".

Industry observers note that "I read somewhere where someone stated something that stuck in my head," he mused, paraphrasing Oscar Wilde's The Portrait of Dorian Gray. "There are many people who know the price of everything but the value of nothing. And I certainly hope that's not where we're going.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • All good things must come to an end implement usage limits.
  • Just a few months after Apple finally launched the long-awaited Siri AI, its upgraded voice assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, the firm will now implement daily usage limits.
  • It has been revealed that what does this mean?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All good things must come to an end implement usage limits.

Just a few months after Apple finally launched the long-awaited Siri AI, its upgraded voice assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, the firm will now implement daily usage limits. These newly introduced restrictions will be implemented along with the launch of iOS 27.3.

It has been revealed that what does this mean? Basically, if a user hits those limits, they will need to upgrade their paid iCloud+ account or wait for the daily limits to reset. However, not every Siri AI request counts towards customers' daily limits.

Recent findings suggest that so, what counts towards your daily Siri AI limits? How much does it cost to upgrade? Lets break down everything you need to know about the new Siri AI usage limits.

According to Apple, "Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for users with a supported device set to a supported language." However, "some features rely on powerful server models and have limits.".

Apple says the following features will have daily usage limits:.

Images: Intelligent Photo Editing Tools, which include Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing, as well as Image Playground.

Workflows and automation: AFM Cloud and AFM Cloud Pro models in Shortcuts.

Third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute.

Apple has not published exactly what the daily usage limits are for Apple Intelligence or Siri AI. The organization's Support page simply describes it as a "generous daily usage limit.".

Notably, each of those above categories has its own unique daily usage limits. These are not shared between those features, which means a user can hit the daily limit for one but not the others.

Daily usage limits are connected at the Apple account level and are implemented across all Apple devices, including iOS devices, Mac, and Apple TV.

When a user reaches their daily limit, they will receive a prompt after making a request that counts towards those limits. Advanced requests are paused until the daily limit resets or the user upgrades to an iCloud+ blueprint.

It has been revealed that "Daily Request Limit Reached," the prompt reads on iOS. "You can continue with basic requests.".

The prompt also includes a button to upgrade to an iCloud+ plan to increase those daily limits.

As previously mentioned, Apple isn't sharing exactly what those Apple Intelligence and Siri AI limits are. However, they have shared just how many times those "generous" limits are increased when upgrading to an iCloud+ initiative.

Sources indicate that here's an outline of what you get with each iCloud+ plan: The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

200GB: $2.99 per month – Up to 2x daily usage limit.

2TB: $9.99 per month – Up to 5x daily usage limit.

6TB: $29.99 per month – Up to 10x daily usage limit.

12TB: $59.99 per month – Up to 20x daily usage limit.

The 50GB iCloud+ plan, which Apple sells for $0.99 per month, does not include any increase in daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.

Apple notes that all feature categories will have their daily limits reset at approximately midnight in the user's current time zone.

According to recent reports, according to Apple, users who are travelling internationally will have their limits reset "around midnight in the central time zone of the country or region of your Apple Account." Users who share an iCloud+ strategy with a Family Sharing group will see their limits reset at around midnight of the time zone of the iCloud+ plan purchaser. Users who aren't signed into their Apple Account will see their limits reset around 24 hours after they first used that feature category that day.

Unused limits from the previous day do not roll over.

Starting with iOS 27.3, Siri AI will also receive limits for certain "advanced" tasks. Apple notes that basic tasks will continue to be unlimited and will work even when the daily usage limits for advanced tasks are reached.

You may be wondering what a "basic" task is and what is an "advanced" task, the latter of which will have daily usage limits.

Apple provided the following examples as a basic task, which users will be able to utilize without limits:.

"Set a timer for three minutes.".

"Text Mark that Annika's party is at 123 Main Street.”.

As for advanced tasks, Apple provides these examples:.

"Text Mark the address for Annika's party, and tell him what time we need to leave from home to make it on time.".

"Add a summary of my San Francisco trip note to this email draft.".

Based on those examples, it appears advanced tasks involve multi-step requests that require server-side processing.

Beyond Apple's official published examples, Apple leaker pdfu has uncovered Apple's more detailed instructions given to Siri AI telling the assistant how to decide if a user has reached their limits for advanced tasks. In an X post, the leaker explained Siri will take limits into account if a user request:.

uses information from one app, from what is on screen or from a message, in a different app, or needs a result from one step used in a different step or app (such as a looked-up fact typed into a field).

contains two or more separate asks in one sentence, even in the same app (extra details of one action, such as a cc or a time, are still one ask).

asks about or summarizes the content of a photo, a camera view or an attachment (editing, searching and albums are fine).

deletes, archives, junks, moves, marks or changes a set (all, every, these or a whole category) of the user’s emails, notes, reminders, messages, photos, files, contacts or events.

sets a device action or a notification to run on a time or trigger (not alarms, timers, reminders or calendar events), notifies someone when a person arrives or leaves, or builds or edits a Shortcut or automation.

is deep research or a multi-step task done on the user’s behalf.

asks you to compose or create fresh content (a story, poem, essay, initiative, recipe, image, or an email or message from a topic rather than wording the user gives), or to rewrite in a tone other than friendly, professional or concise.

A user asking a third-party AI assistant like ChatGPT for an advanced request is never limited, even if a user reaches their daily usage limit for the day.

According to pdfu, tasks like "proofreading, rewriting in a friendly, professional or concise tone, summaries as key points, a list or a table, typing or sending wording the user gives, a single direct operation in any app, even when Siri must look the target up first (the closest bakery, my cousin), 'this' or 'that' within its own app, running a Shortcut by name, a reminder for yourself by time or place, Find My, sharing your ETA or location, and all your home accessories (lights, doors, locks), alarms, timers or device settings" all fall under basic tasks.

So far, Apple hasn't released much more on these new daily usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Hopefully, before iOS 27.3 comes out, Apple provides consumers with more specific information regarding what does and doesn't count towards their daily usage limits.

  • The San Francisco-based artificial intelligence firm published a lengthy blog post this week claiming that its Claude Fable 5.2 model had made some progress on figuring out two long-standing mysteries surrounding black holes.
  • According to Anthropic, the first conundrum Claude was able to solve involved the concept of heating up a hypothetical universe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At a time when Anthropic is vacuuming up stock market money, the AI company has made a pretty grandiose claim about its Claude chatbot's scientific capabilities.

The San Francisco-based artificial intelligence firm published a lengthy blog post this week claiming that its Claude Fable 5.2 model had made some progress on figuring out two long-standing mysteries surrounding black holes. The post goes into an incredible amount of scientific detail that might fly over your head (as much of it did mine), but I'll try my best to summarize it in plain English.

According to Anthropic, the first conundrum Claude was able to solve involved the concept of heating up a hypothetical universe. When the universe reaches a certain temperature, it would form a black hole through a sudden "phase transition," as initially described by Stephen Hawking and Don Page in 1983. Hawking and Page's findings concerned only a vast universe described by general relativity, while this theoretical universe is much smaller and might work differently.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

It turns out, as Claude found, that the phase transition is also abrupt in a smaller universe. As Anthropic explained, this implies that "black hole formation isn’t just a feature of relativity but is actually built into the underlying quantum theory.".

As for the second finding, it revolves around another theoretical universe made up of two dimensions instead of three. In this universe, physicists have spent years trying to figure out how heavy the lightest possible black hole could be using a technique called "bootstrapping," in which the ceiling for the lightest black hole gets lowered each time a theory breaks it. Anthropic claimed that Claude Fable 5.2 was able to notice a pattern that physicists had missed in their calculations and use it to "calculate the precise ceiling for the simplest version of this technique and prove that it could not be lowered.".

It has been revealed that as Anthropic was quick to point out in the blog post, these findings do not apply to our universe or have any practical application but could give us an idea of how relativity and quantum mechanics work together. It's also worth noting that these findings were released alongside Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO, AKA a time when Anthropic wants as much public money as possible.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google is giving its fledgling Googlebook OS a hefty dose of desktop polish with the rollout of Chrome 157.
  • Industry observers note that since the launch of Googlebook for consumers earlier this fall, Google has been slowly smoothing out the rough edges of its latest Android-meets-desktop platform.
  • Recent findings suggest that the biggest changes are aimed at those who favor vertical tabs over Chrome’s traditional horizontal layout.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is giving its fledgling Googlebook OS a hefty dose of desktop polish with the rollout of Chrome 157. The company has published the full changelog for the browser update, which includes five major features and 22 under-the-hood fixes.

Industry observers note that since the launch of Googlebook for consumers earlier this fall, Google has been slowly smoothing out the rough edges of its latest Android-meets-desktop platform. With Chrome 157 being the primary interface on Googlebook OS, the little desktop quirks — a right-click menu that doesn’t work correctly or a tab rail that refuses to stay fully extended — appear even more glaring than they would on a traditional laptop. This release directly addresses those day-to-day friction points.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest changes are aimed at those who favor vertical tabs over Chrome’s traditional horizontal layout. Before, if a vertical tab rail collapsed, it was difficult to tell which pages were open without expanding the entire sidebar. That’s what Chrome 157 fixes with Auto-Expand Vertical Tabs on Hover, which pops open the rail temporarily when you hover over it with your mouse or trackpad. You move away, and it drops down again.

According to recent reports, you can also resize the vertical tab bar by hand to allow for longer page titles. This option requires you to disable auto expansion, but Chrome remembers your preferred width between browser restarts and newly introduced windows.

Recent findings suggest that google has also simplified navigation of Chrome’s Settings. You can now bookmark or share individual sections such as Appearance and Privacy, as each settings page has its own URL. The browser’s Back and Forward buttons also function when navigating between settings pages.

It has been revealed that chrome 157 adds a persistent control bar when sharing browser tabs during video calls. If you’re presenting via Google Meet, you can stop sharing or switch to another tab without having to dig through menus.

The system's native Save As dialog is enabled by default for actions like saving images, links, and webpages. You have more control over the file names and destinations, including Google Drive and external storage.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

In a recent development, the other 22 improvements cover minor irritations. Right-click the address bar, and you get the standard desktop text editing menu. Press Ctrl+L and you get the entire URL with parameters. Chrome also fixes bookmark context menus, improves PDF translation, and allows downloaded PDFs to open directly in a browser tab.

Sources indicate that other fixes include external monitor selection for Google Slides, Picture-in-Picture media controls, web app navigation, and third-party Google Sign-In prompts that might freeze when dismissed. Contextual Search also receives a less intrusive privacy notice.

This massive enhancement comes after last week's broader Chrome 157 launch and a huge system patch in November. The update doesn’t come with a slew of flashy additions, but its suite of practical fixes should make Google’s browser more comfortable to use.

Recent findings suggest that chinese Android brands like Oppo, Vivo, Xiaomi, Realme, and several others often outshine Western brands in many ways, but they’ve always had one annoying weakness: software. Whether it’s the number of updates a phone receives, overall quality, or another specific concern, Chinese brands often build very different visions of Android than Google, Samsung, Motorola, or Nothing.

Industry observers note that the value and hardware prowess these phones usually deliver help outshine software weaknesses, and these companies have been steadily improving software over the past year or two to meet the demands of a more Westernized audience. Companies like Honor now offer 7 years of software updates, and ColorOS is widely regarded as the best Android skin next to Samsung’s One UI in many circles. That’s great news for everyone, especially in an age where fewer smartphone companies compete for your hard-earned dollars.

Motorola has posted an updated list of devices getting its Android 17 enhancement, with a few updates already available and many more left to go.

With the upgrade now rolling out to select devices, most recently the Razr Fold, Motorola is confirming an official list of devices getting Android 17.

Recent findings suggest that the list was posted by Motorola Brazil, so this includes devices Motorola doesn’t sell in US markets, and also lists Razr devices without their year naming scheme, rather their international branding – i.e. “Razr (2026)” is “Razr 70.”.

As per usual, Motorola’s update rollouts may see timing vary by region. The Razr Fold update, for example, is currently rolling out in some international markets but has yet to land in the US.

Here’s the full list of Motorola devices officially confirmed to be getting Android 17:.

Motorola explains what’s latest in Android 17 as follows:.

It has been revealed that among the newly introduced features of Android 17 are improvements to the system interface, with more customization options, new icons, and changes to the layout of buttons and widgets. The Settings menu has been redesigned to make navigation more intuitive and facilitate access to the smartphone’s main functions.

Artificial intelligence in everyday life.

With the enhancement, Circle to Search now offers real-time translations, allowing you to understand content in other languages ​​more easily, without having to interrupt your current activity on your smartphone.

Simplified connectivity and sharing.

Android 17 enhances connectivity with Instant Hotspot , which simplifies sharing your internet connection between compatible devices. Quick Share has also received improvements to facilitate file transfer, including compatibility with iOS smartphones via QR Code.

Sources indicate that security remains a top priority for the system. The Authentication Failure Lock , a security feature in case of theft, locks the screen after unsuccessful authentication attempts. Meanwhile, Message-Based Fraud Detection enhances the identification of potential threats and fraud. Furthermore, access to emergency calls has become easier and faster.

More control over the visual experience.

In a recent development, the update also improves HDR brightness control, which adjusts the screen intensity to highlight bright details in compatible photos and videos. People can adjust this brightness for more comfortable viewing, or even disable the feature.

The Motorola Signature 27, the company’s new flagship, ships with Android 17 out of the box.
